records.label: Close eye-level viewpoint
records.visual_function: Create conversational proximity through an eye-level camera that keeps facial proportions stable and makes subtle performance easy to read.
records.prompt: Use an eye-level close portrait viewpoint with natural facial perspective, a comfortable head-and-shoulders distance, restrained lens expansion, and a direct spatial relationship between the subject's eyes and the viewer.
invariants: camera height aligns near the subject's eye line
facial landmarks retain natural relative proportions
the chosen crop supports readable eyes and mouth
misreadings_to_avoid: telephoto flattening that removes spatial presence
wide-lens facial distortion
camera height drifting into a strong high or low angle

records.label: Low three-quarter viewpoint
records.visual_function: Convey grounded physical presence with a moderate low camera and a three-quarter turn that keeps facial identity and torso structure readable.
records.prompt: Set the camera modestly below the face in a three-quarter view, enlarging the near shoulder slightly, keeping both eyes structurally coherent, and allowing the torso to rise through the frame with stable perspective.
invariants: the low angle remains moderate enough for facial readability
near and far features follow one perspective system
the three-quarter turn preserves a clear muzzle or facial silhouette
misreadings_to_avoid: extreme under-chin view
uncontrolled shoulder enlargement
frontal face pasted onto a rotated head

records.label: Profile framing with open space
records.visual_function: Frame a side-facing subject with enough open image area to extend attention beyond the body and support a reserved narrative tone.
records.prompt: Use a clean side or near-profile camera position, place the visible eye and facial contour as the main landmarks, and leave an intentional field of image space forward of the subject's attention.
invariants: the facial contour remains a strong identity-bearing shape
open space follows the directional logic of the gaze
camera placement keeps the visible eye structurally seated
misreadings_to_avoid: ambiguous almost-frontal head rotation
gaze directed into the nearest frame edge
flattened facial contour with lost muzzle or nose structure

records.label: Environmental medium portrait
records.visual_function: Show character and setting together through a medium portrait distance that preserves facial performance while revealing meaningful environmental context.
records.prompt: Frame the subject from roughly waist or mid-torso upward, retain a readable face, include one foreground or side-plane cue, and reveal enough background structure to establish place and depth around the character.
invariants: the face remains readable at the selected image scale
environment cues establish place through clear depth layers
the subject silhouette stays distinct from nearby background forms
misreadings_to_avoid: wide establishing shot with a tiny face
background clutter equal to subject detail
random crop that conceals the character's activity

records.label: High angle looking down
records.visual_function: Place the camera above the subject looking down to soften presence, add vulnerability, or show layout.
records.prompt: Shoot from a high angle: the camera clearly above the subject pitching downward, the subject's upper surfaces and foreshortened body visible, the ground plane rising behind them as backdrop, and a gentle sense of smallness or openness in their presence.
invariants: the camera height stays clearly above the subject
downward pitch matches the visible ground backdrop
foreshortening compresses the body believably
misreadings_to_avoid: eye-level proportions contradicting the stated height
background sky where the ground should rise
distorted head enlargement past believable perspective

records.label: Bird's-eye top-down view
records.visual_function: Look straight down from far above so the scene flattens into graphic shapes and patterns.
records.prompt: Shoot from a bird's-eye view: the camera almost perpendicular above the scene looking straight down, bodies and objects flattened into readable graphic shapes, shadows acting as design elements, and floor or ground texture serving as the composition field.
invariants: the view stays near-perpendicular to the ground
the ground plane fills the frame as the field
subjects read as clear top-down silhouettes
misreadings_to_avoid: three-quarter aerial tilt sneaking in a horizon
eye-level anatomy pasted onto a top-down floor
shadows contradicting the single overhead reading

records.label: Worm's-eye ground-level upward
records.visual_function: Shoot from ground level steeply upward so the subject towers with extreme dominance.
records.prompt: Shoot from a worm's-eye view: the camera at or near the ground pointing steeply upward, the subject towering with strong vertical convergence, near forms such as feet or legs greatly enlarged, and sky or ceiling as the backdrop behind the figure.
invariants: the camera sits at ground level pitching steeply up
vertical lines converge upward consistently
near lower-body forms enlarge ahead of the head
misreadings_to_avoid: level-camera proportions without upward convergence
ground backdrop where sky or ceiling belongs
the head enlarged instead of the near lower body

records.label: First-person point of view
records.visual_function: Show the scene through a participant's eyes, with their own body entering the frame edges naturally.
records.prompt: Shoot as a first-person point of view: the camera at the viewer-character's eye position, their own hands, arms, or knees entering from the frame edges when they act, subjects addressing the lens as if meeting the viewer's eyes, and natural human eye-height perspective on the scene.
invariants: the camera occupies a participant's eye position
any visible own-body parts enter from frame edges
other subjects relate to the lens as to a person
misreadings_to_avoid: floating third-person distance contradicting the POV
own-body parts detached from the frame edges
subjects' eye-lines missing the lens without reason
